How it works

Background: top view rendered from the Unreal Engine scene (north up, 0.5 m per pixel), GPS traces of 116 recording sessions (dots coloured by driving direction), concrete slabs, buildings and trees as placed in the UE5 scene, and the static recording positions (pods W/F/T/O). When Snap is on, path points snap to the GPS traces: click points in driving order; the direction is inferred from the points.

Static ego: “Place on map”, then one click for the position and a second click for the viewing direction (cam1). Driving ego: drawn path (clicks, double-click to finish) or a named road of zone O. With per-point speeds, the speed varies linearly from one point to the next (exported as points every metre); a last point at 0 km/h = gradual stop.

Any number can become a range ± (min–max): the generator draws one value per variant. Variants = number of scenes produced (random draws within the ranges and model lists: name_01, name_02…). Preview = what the map shows: every range at its midpoint, one specific draw (the same as in production), or the mirrored version.

Mirrored version: when ticked, the same draws are also produced with every vehicle driving the same path in reverse (overtaking / oncoming: opposite side; following: ahead ↔ behind); these scenes are named name_mirror_01…; the ego does not change.

Lanes (blue/red layer): the axis of each driving direction, extracted from the GPS traces (median of all passes); the catalogue paths follow them. Named roads (dashed orange): the taxiway / ramp / connector axes used by the driving ego and by relative motions. Landmarks: T-junction stations at 10/50/100 m (squares) and pods. Objects: buildings (brown rectangles) and trees (green discs) as placed in the UE5 scene.

The strips at the bottom preview the per-second label of each vehicle seen from the ego (front / left / right / back). “Export JSON” gives the scenario file for the simulation pipeline.

Workflow

1. Draw or load a scenario; set speeds, distances, ranges and variants. 2. “Export JSON” and pass the file to the scenario generator, which produces one scene per variant (plus the mirrored ones if enabled).

Coordinates are in a local East-North frame derived from GPS (ENU, anchor 53.174452 N / 8.168086 E), in metres; headings are mathematical angles (0° = east, 90° = north). The concrete slabs and the UE5 scene of zone O are offset by (−20.3; +50.9) m from this frame; the simulation applies this transform automatically.
